title: What’s Your Favourite Kind Of Noodle?

blanks.sentence: They were carried along an ancient trade route by _____.
Local versions were shaped by _____ and new ingredients.
In the 1920s and 30s, noodles in the US were seen as _____.
A food-industry organisation wanted to promote the making of _____.
The story about a famous traveller was designed to _____.
Ramen was influenced by _____ who had moved to Japan.
Japanese chefs changed the imported dishes, including by adding _____.
Compared with many traditional foods, ramen still _____.

multipleChoice.question: What is the main point made about noodles in the opening topic discussion?
options: They became popular because modern packets made them convenient.
Their history is mainly a story of one country exporting one recipe.
They spread across places and were repeatedly adapted by local cooks.
Their appeal depends more on ingredients than on cultural exchange.

multipleChoice.question: Why was the Marco Polo story promoted in the United States?
options: It helped market dried pasta by giving it an attractive origin story.
It corrected a historical error about European noodle-making.
It explained why Asian noodles had disappeared from America.
It proved that dried pasta was invented in thirteenth-century Italy.

multipleChoice.question: What is the attitude toward the claim that pasta came from Marco Polo’s trip?
options: It is treated as a confirmed discovery with broad evidence.
It is presented as a harmless legend with no commercial purpose.
It is accepted only for explaining Italian cooking traditions.
It is rejected as a story created to promote pasta sales.

multipleChoice.question: According to the explanation, what happened after the promotional story was used?
options: People became less interested in imported Asian noodles.
Pasta sales increased because the story served its purpose.
Pasta makers stopped focusing on dried pasta production.
American consumers demanded only fresh wheat noodles.

multipleChoice.question: How did Chinese noodle dishes become more Japanese?
options: Chefs kept their basic appeal but adjusted them for local tastes.
Chefs replaced noodles with sushi-style ingredients.
Chefs removed foreign influences to preserve tradition.
Chefs copied Chinese recipes without changing them.

multipleChoice.question: What does the ramen enthusiast seem to value most about ramen?
options: Its close connection with one unchanged recipe.
Its status as the oldest Japanese noodle dish.
Its ability to keep developing beyond fixed norms.
Its simple preparation using packet noodles only.

multipleChoice.question: In the chef’s comment, what does “these dishes” most probably refer to?
options: Modern versions of dried pasta in America.
Toppings added to instant noodle packets.
Traditional foods such as sushi and hotpot.
Chinese noodle dishes that inspired ramen.

multipleChoice.question: What can be inferred about the Japanese chefs who adapted the dishes?
options: They viewed Chinese noodles as unsuitable for Japan.
They admired them but wanted a more local version.
They were trying to reproduce Italian pasta culture.
They wanted ramen to stop changing over time.

multipleChoice.question: Why are toppings and slices of meat mentioned?
options: To show practical examples of changes that shaped ramen.
To argue that ramen became less Japanese over time.
To compare ramen with dried pasta manufacturing.
To explain why noodles no longer link to the past.

multipleChoice.question: What is the broader implication of the noodle examples?
options: Food history becomes reliable only when linked to famous travellers.
Successful noodle dishes usually reject earlier cultural influences.
Noodle traditions often survive by changing as they move between cultures.
Modern convenience has ended the need for traditional flavours.
